plans.objective: [DIM: composition] The solution space of rigid constraint families is invariant under scaling of the training set size w, as the analytical ground truth (e.g., y = x) defines a unique function independent of sample density. This hypothesis is testable via the linear family (y = x) and the fat family (random polynomials), with clear predictions for N_c(w) trends.

steps.description: Implement the `family` function to generate data for the linear family (y=x, rigid) and random polynomial family (fat). Ensure data is normalized to O(1) magnitude to satisfy the strict zero-violation criterion (max abs error ≤ 1e-3). Generate training points X/y and held-out points Xv/yv with no overlap, reshape to (N,1), and return as a dictionary. This enables the capacity_scan tool to test the hypothesis that N_c(w) is finite and flat for linear, but unreachable for fat families.

plans.objective: [DIM: structure] The rigidity of the solution space is fundamentally determined by the topological connectivity of the constraint graph rather than the algebraic form of the constraints; specifically, if the constraint graph contains cycles, the solution space becomes locally convex (rigid), whereas a tree structure preserves fatness.

steps.description: Implement the constraint families (rigid linear family and fat random polynomial family) as the `family` function, ensuring outputs are normalized to O(1) and held-out points are disjoint from training points. steps.description: The hypothesis that solution-space rigidity maps to constraint-graph connectivity requires empirical testing via bootstrap probing of small neural networks. We will implement a capacity-scan workflow: define two constraint families (rigid: linear; fat: high-degree polynomial), normalize outputs to O(1), and run capacity_scan with width scan h∈[2,64], w=10 samples, 3 seeds. We will verify the rigidity anchor (≤1e3 heldout error at small h) and check if fat family remains unreachable (unreachable trend). This tests whether network capacity serves as a valid rigidity probe.
